disclaimer: Reference fixture in the simulator trace schema (v4). The scenarios are written by hand, but every function, theorem, predicate, right, syscall number and error they name is the kernel's own: the sync resolves each declaration in the pinned seLe4n checkout and fails if one is missing. The validator re-runs every capability lookup, type check, rights check, flow check and scheduling decision against the state, recomputes every timer tick, reschedule and interrupt whole, and refuses a trace that disagrees. The kernel does not yet export JSON traces; when it does (source == "kernel"), steps become a replay of a real run.

propertyCatalog.label: No capability, no access
propertyCatalog.statement: A syscall reaches its operation only after the caller's CSpace resolves the named slot to a capability of the kind that syscall acts on, carrying the right it requires; the gate itself changes no state.

propertyCatalog.label: Derived authority never grows
propertyCatalog.statement: A minted or copied capability names the same object as its parent and carries a subset of the parent's rights: the rights asked for are masked by the parent's, so a derivation can only lose them.

propertyCatalog.label: A refused syscall changes nothing
propertyCatalog.statement: A kernel transition has type SystemState → Except KernelError (α × SystemState): an error carries no successor state, so every refusal leaves the system exactly as it was.
propertyCatalog.caveat: This holds by the type of a transition rather than by a separate theorem.

propertyCatalog.label: Non-interference
propertyCatalog.statement: Every NonInterferenceStep, and every trace of them, preserves low-equivalence: what an observer at one security level can see does not depend on higher-level state.
propertyCatalog.caveat: Stated over the NonInterferenceStep relation, one constructor per kernel step. The theorem over the live checked syscall entry holds given a per-arm hypothesis.

propertyCatalog.label: IPC never flows down the lattice
propertyCatalog.statement: The endpoint flow gate admits a message only if the global security lattice allows the flow from sender to receiver; an endpoint override can narrow that, never widen it.

propertyCatalog.label: Memory isolation
propertyCatalog.statement: Carving from untyped memory preserves the untyped-memory invariant: free indexes stay inside their regions and carved children never overlap. Distinct address-space roots carry distinct ASIDs.

propertyCatalog.label: W^X: no page is writable and executable
propertyCatalog.statement: Any successful mapping was given W^X-compliant permissions: the argument decoder (PagePermissions.ofNat?) refuses a writable and executable permission word, so no page table entry is ever written with both.

propertyCatalog.label: Invariant preservation
propertyCatalog.statement: The syscall entry preserves proofLayerInvariantBundle, the composition of every subsystem invariant.
propertyCatalog.caveat: Compositional: the theorem takes, as a hypothesis, that the dispatched operation preserves the bundle, and per-operation preservation theorems discharge it arm by arm.

propertyCatalog.label: Scheduling discipline
propertyCatalog.statement: The per-core selector picks the best thread of the highest-priority bucket (priority, then earliest deadline, then FIFO), and a scheduling context is never charged more than its budget in any window of one period.
propertyCatalog.caveat: Optimality is stated over the maximum-priority bucket, not the whole queue; the budget bound is stated over the context's refill events. There is no unconditional no-starvation theorem.

propertyCatalog.label: Budget replenishment
propertyCatalog.statement: A budget that is used returns exactly one period after the refill it came from was released, and only through the release queue: a charge never leaves a refill due in the past, the queue stays sorted by release time, and a tick keeps every pending refill on it.
propertyCatalog.caveat: These are statements about the refill bookkeeping. The bound on how long a thread runs is the scheduling property's refill_window_bound.

propertyCatalog.label: Interrupt delivery
propertyCatalog.statement: A device interrupt reaches only the notification whose capability the line's handler bound, carries that capability's badge, and leaves the line masked until the handler acknowledges it.
propertyCatalog.caveat: At this revision the kernel states no invariant of its own over interrupt lines, so the page checks none. The theorems cited are about the operations: what a bound line names, and what an acknowledge writes.

invariantCatalog.label: Endpoint queues well-formed
invariantCatalog.meaning: Every endpoint's send and receive queues are well-formed intrusive lists whose members are blocked on that endpoint.

invariantCatalog.label: No thread queued twice
invariantCatalog.meaning: No thread appears twice in an endpoint queue.

invariantCatalog.label: Blocked threads are not runnable
invariantCatalog.meaning: A thread blocked on send, receive, reply or a notification is never in a run queue.

invariantCatalog.label: Notification waiters consistent
invariantCatalog.meaning: A notification's waiter list holds exactly the threads blocked on it.

invariantCatalog.label: Reply waiters consistent
invariantCatalog.meaning: A thread blocked on a reply waits on another live thread, and a reply object names its caller only while that caller is blocked on the reply.

invariantCatalog.label: Running thread is not queued
invariantCatalog.meaning: The thread a core is running is not also in its run queue.

invariantCatalog.label: Current thread is a TCB
invariantCatalog.meaning: Whatever a core records as its current thread is a thread control block in the object store.

invariantCatalog.label: Budget within bounds
invariantCatalog.meaning: A scheduling context's remaining budget never exceeds its configured budget, and its budget never exceeds its period.

invariantCatalog.label: Derivation links agree
invariantCatalog.meaning: Every derivation link joins two occupied slots, and each slot has at most one parent: the tree the kernel walks to revoke is the tree the slots describe.

invariantCatalog.label: Derivation tree acyclic
invariantCatalog.meaning: No capability is derived, directly or transitively, from itself.

invariantCatalog.label: Untyped free index in bounds
invariantCatalog.meaning: The free index of every untyped capability stays inside the region it names.

invariantCatalog.label: Carved objects never overlap
invariantCatalog.meaning: The children carved from one untyped occupy disjoint memory.

invariantCatalog.label: No writable+executable page
invariantCatalog.meaning: No mapping in any address space is both writable and executable.

invariantCatalog.label: ASIDs unique
invariantCatalog.meaning: Each ASID names at most one address-space root.

invariantCatalog.label: No stale TLB entries
invariantCatalog.meaning: Every cached translation corresponds to a live mapping; an unmap shoots the entry down.

invariantCatalog.label: Audit log bounded
invariantCatalog.meaning: The declassification audit trail never exceeds its capacity; a full trail refuses the downgrade.

invariantCatalog.label: No refill is lost or stranded
invariantCatalog.meaning: A scheduling context's head and pending refills always sum to its budget, and a used-up context that a thread holds, with a refill still pending, is on a release queue at that refill's release time. Nothing else would ever release it: the tick reads the queues alone.

scenarios.title: Call and reply through an endpoint
scenarios.summary: A server waits on an endpoint with a reply object; a client calls it, the server answers through the reply object, and the client resumes with the answer. Every hop is a queue operation on the kernel's own objects.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The server (priority 120) runs on core 0 and the client (priority 100) waits in the run queue. The server holds the endpoint with read, write and grant, and a reply object; the client holds the same endpoint with write only, minted with badge 17, so the server can tell which client is calling.

steps.title: server: receive on the endpoint

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the endpoint)
Check the capability's type: receive invokes an endpoint
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; no sender waits, so block with the reply object stashed

steps.narrative: x0 = 1 walks the server's CSpace to slot 1, the endpoint capability, which carries the read right a receive needs. The flow gate admits endpoint → server. Because msgInfo.length is 1, x2 names a reply object: slot 2 resolves to it. No sender is queued, so the server joins the endpoint's receive queue, stashes the reply object for the next caller, and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: pick the next thread
steps.narrative: The server left the core, so on the way out of the kernel the scheduler picks again. The client is the only runnable thread, so it is dispatched and leaves the run queue (a running thread is never queued).

steps.title: client: call the service

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the badged endpoint)
Check the capability's type: call invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Caller → endpoint flow gate
Rendezvous with the waiting server, then block on the reply

steps.narrative: The client's slot 1 holds the endpoint with write, which a call needs. The flow gate admits client → endpoint. The server is waiting, so the kernel pops it off the receive queue and hands it the two message words, the label and the capability's badge, 17. The server becomes runnable on its home core. The client blocks on the reply, and the server's stashed reply object now names the client as its caller.

steps.title: core 0: pick the next thread
steps.narrative: The client blocked, so core 0 picks again: the server is the only runnable thread.

steps.title: server: reply

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, the reply object)
Check the capability's type: reply invokes a reply capability
Require the write right
Transfer the reply to the caller the reply object names

steps.narrative: The reply resolves through the reply object, not through the endpoint: slot 2 names rp.svc, and rp.svc names the client. The kernel checks server → client against the flow policy (a refusal here would be replyCapInvalid, not flowDenied), delivers the reply word, unlinks the caller from the reply object and wakes the client. The server keeps the core: the client's priority is lower, so nothing preempts it.

steps.title: server: receive again

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the endpoint)
Check the capability's type: receive invokes an endpoint
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; no sender waits, so block

steps.narrative: The server goes back to waiting for the next call, with the same reply object, which is free again.

steps.title: core 0: the client resumes
steps.narrative: The client is dispatched and returns from its call with the server's answer, 49, in its first message register.

scenarios.title: The capability gate
scenarios.summary: Four syscalls from a thread holding one read-only endpoint capability. Three are refused, at the stage that refuses them and with the error it returns; each refusal leaves the state exactly as it was.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The app thread's CSpace is a 16-slot CNode with a 4-bit guard of 0, so a CPtr's low 8 bits are its address: the top 4 must match the guard and the bottom 4 pick the slot. Slot 1 holds an endpoint capability with the read right only.

steps.title: app: send with a read-only capability

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Check the capability's type: send invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send

steps.narrative: x0 = 1 resolves: guard 0 matches and slot 1 holds the endpoint. But a send needs write and the capability carries only read. An IPC syscall answers a missing right the way it answers a missing capability, with invalidCapability, so a caller cannot tell a slot it may not use from one that holds nothing. Nothing after the gate runs and nothing changes.

steps.title: app: call through an empty slot

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 5)
Check the capability's type: call invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Caller → endpoint flow gate
Call

steps.narrative: x0 = 5: the guard matches, but slot 5 is empty. There is no capability to check, so the lookup refuses with invalidCapability: the same answer the read-only capability got.

steps.title: app: send through a guard mismatch

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (guard 3, slot 1)
Check the capability's type: send invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send

steps.narrative: x0 = 0x31: the low 4 bits select slot 1, which is occupied, but the 4 bits above them read 3 and the CNode's guard is 0. A CPtr whose guard does not match resolves to nothing, so the lookup refuses before it ever reads the slot.

steps.title: app: receive, which the capability allows

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Check the capability's type: receive invokes an endpoint
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; nothing is queued, so block

steps.narrative: The same capability does carry read, which is what a receive needs. msgInfo.length is 0, so the receive names no reply object. Nothing is queued on the endpoint, so the app blocks on it and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: nothing to run
steps.narrative: No thread is runnable, so core 0 runs nothing until an interrupt or another core wakes something.

scenarios.title: Notifications: signals and badges
scenarios.summary: A driver signals a handler through three badged capabilities. A signal carries the badge of the capability it was sent through, never a word the caller supplies. The first wakes the waiting handler; the next two find nobody waiting and accumulate as a bitwise OR in the notification word, which the handler collects in one wait.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The handler is blocked on the alarm notification. The driver runs; both have priority 80. The driver holds three capabilities that can signal (write), badged 0b001, 0b100 and 0b010: one per source it reports. The handler's capability can wait (read).

steps.title: driver: signal through slot 1 (badge 0b001)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Check the capability's type: notificationSignal invokes a notification
Require the write right
Signaller → notification flow gate
Signal

steps.narrative: A signal sends no message words: the badge is the one minted into the capability in slot 1. The handler is waiting, so the badge does not touch the notification word: the kernel pops the handler off the wait queue and delivers badge 1 straight to it, after checking that the flow onward to the handler is allowed too. The handler becomes runnable but does not preempt the driver: equal priority never does.

steps.title: driver: signal through slot 2 (badge 0b100)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, the notification)
Check the capability's type: notificationSignal invokes a notification
Require the write right
Signaller → notification flow gate
Signal

steps.narrative: Nobody waits now, so the badge of the capability in slot 2 is stored: the notification becomes active with word 0b100.

steps.title: driver: signal through slot 3 (badge 0b010)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 3, the notification)
Check the capability's type: notificationSignal invokes a notification
Require the write right
Signaller → notification flow gate
Signal

steps.narrative: A second signal with nobody waiting ORs its capability's badge into the word: 0b100 | 0b010 = 0b110. Signals coalesce; the word records which sources fired, not how often.

steps.title: driver: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Charge the rest of the slice, requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: Yield names no capability, so the path goes straight from decode to the scheduler. The driver's time slice is reset and it goes to the tail of its priority bucket, behind the handler, which the scheduler then picks.

steps.title: handler: wait, collecting 0b110

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Check the capability's type: notificationWait invokes a notification
Require the read right
Notification → waiter flow gate
Wait; the word is set, so take it without blocking

steps.narrative: The notification is active, so the wait returns at once with the accumulated word, 0b110, and clears it. The handler learns that sources 1 and 2 both fired.

steps.title: handler: wait again

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the notification)
Check the capability's type: notificationWait invokes a notification
Require the read right
Notification → waiter flow gate
Wait; the word is clear, so block

steps.narrative: Nothing is pending, so the handler joins the wait queue and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: the driver resumes
steps.narrative: The handler blocked, so the driver, the only runnable thread, is dispatched.

scenarios.title: Priority buckets and round robin
scenarios.summary: Three threads share priority 50 and one sits at 10. Timer ticks spend the running thread's slice; when it runs out the thread goes to the tail of its bucket and the head of the highest bucket runs. The priority-10 thread never runs while a priority-50 thread can.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: Thread a runs with 2 ticks left of its slice. b and c wait in the priority-50 bucket, d in the priority-10 bucket. The run queue keeps insertion order within each bucket.

steps.title: tick: a has 1 tick left
steps.narrative: A timer tick charges the running thread one tick of its slice. a has 1 left and keeps the core.

steps.title: tick: a's slice runs out
steps.narrative: The tick finds a on its last tick. Its slice is refilled to 5 and it goes to the tail of the priority-50 bucket, behind b and c. The scheduler scans the highest bucket in order and takes its head, b. d is not considered: the bucket above it has runnable threads.

steps.title: b: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Charge the rest of the slice, requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: b gives up the rest of its slice. It is requeued at the tail of its bucket, and the bucket's new head, c, runs.

steps.title: tick: c spends a tick
steps.narrative: c has a fresh slice and spends one tick of it. The bucket now reads a, b behind c; d is still waiting below.

scenarios.title: Budgets, refills and deadlines
scenarios.summary: Three threads at one priority, each bound to a scheduling context, and one unbound thread below them. A tick charges the running context; a context that is used up waits on the release queue until the budget it used comes back, one period after it was released; among the eligible, the earliest deadline wins.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The state the scenario starts from.

steps.title: tick 3: alpha's budget runs out
steps.narrative: alpha has one tick left in its head refill and nothing that would merge into it, so this tick uses the head up (tickExhausts). The tick it ran is scheduled to come back one period after the head was released: 2 + 6 = 8, which touches the refill already pending at 7, so the two join into one refill of 2 at time 7. alpha's context goes on the release queue at 7 and alpha itself goes back on the run queue, where it is ineligible: its budget is 0. Of the eligible threads in the priority-60 bucket, beta is first in the queue but gamma's deadline (5) is earlier than beta's (8), so gamma runs.

steps.title: tick 4: gamma's one-tick budget runs out
steps.narrative: gamma's whole budget is one tick. The head was released at 0 and is taken up at 3 (refill_unblock_check moves a head that was ready to the moment it starts running), so the tick comes back at 3 + 9 = 12. gamma's context joins the release queue behind alpha's. beta is the only eligible thread left at priority 60.

steps.title: tick 5: beta spends a tick
steps.narrative: beta has two ticks, so this tick does not use the head up. One tick is charged: the head shrinks to 1 and the tick that was used is scheduled to return at 4 + 8 = 12, one period after the head started. Nothing else changes; no release is due.

steps.title: tick 6: beta's budget runs out
steps.narrative: beta's last tick would return at 5 + 8 = 13, which touches the refill pending at 12, so the whole budget of 2 returns together at 12. beta's context is placed on the release queue behind the entries released no later than it (alpha at 7, gamma at 12). Every thread in the priority-60 bucket is now out of budget, so the scheduler falls back to a scan of the whole queue and runs the background thread, which is bound to no context and is charged a time slice instead.

steps.title: tick 7: alpha's refill is released
steps.narrative: The tick first drains the release queue: alpha's refill of 2 is due at 7, so it becomes the head again, and a context that was exhausted and holds budget again gets a new deadline one period on, 7 + 6 = 13. alpha is already on the run queue, so nothing is enqueued, but the core's decision is now stale. The running thread is then charged (the background thread's slice goes from 5 to 4), and the scheduling point finds a candidate that outranks it: alpha, at priority 60 against 10. The background thread goes to the tail of the queue and alpha runs.

steps.title: tick 8: alpha spends a tick
steps.narrative: alpha's head was released at 7 and has run since, so the tick it used returns at 7 + 6 = 13.

steps.title: tick 9: alpha is out of budget again
steps.narrative: The second tick would return at 8 + 6 = 14, which touches the refill pending at 13: both return at 13. alpha's context goes on the release queue behind gamma's and beta's, which are due at 12. No bound thread has budget, so the background thread runs again.

steps.title: tick 10: the background thread runs
steps.narrative: Nothing is due on the release queue until 12. The background thread's time slice goes from 4 to 3.

steps.title: tick 11: the background thread runs
steps.narrative: Still nothing due. The slice goes from 3 to 2.

steps.title: tick 12: two refills are released at once
steps.narrative: gamma's and beta's refills are both due at 12, and the drain takes the queue's head while it is due: gamma first, then beta. Each gets a new deadline one period on: gamma 12 + 9 = 21, beta 12 + 8 = 20. After the background thread is charged, the scheduling point compares the best candidate with it. Both refilled threads are eligible at priority 60; beta's deadline is the earlier, so beta preempts the background thread. alpha is still waiting for 13.

scenarios.title: Minting, copying, deleting and revoking
scenarios.summary: A supervisor derives capabilities from an endpoint master capability and then takes them back. Every derivation is recorded in the derivation tree, a derived capability can only lose rights (rights it asks for beyond its source's are masked off, not refused), and revoking the master deletes everything derived from it.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The supervisor's CSpace holds, in slot 0, a capability to the CNode itself (with grant, which minting and copying need) and, in slot 1, the master capability to the log endpoint with read, write and grant. A CNode operation is addressed as seL4's is: x0 names the destination CNode, x2 the destination slot, x3 a capability to the source CNode, x4 the source slot, and x5 packs both lookup depths (8 bits each here) with the rights mask.

steps.title: mint slot 1 → slot 4: write only, badge 7
steps.narrative: The rights mask 0b00010 asks for write alone, which the master holds, so slot 4 receives a write-only capability to the same endpoint and becomes the first child of slot 1 in the derivation tree. A mint carries five words: the fifth, the badge (7), does not fit in x2–x5 and travels in the caller's IPC buffer.

ipcBuffer.name: badge (message word 4; 0 keeps the source badge)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceMint invokes a CNode
Require the grant right
Decode the arm's 5 argument words
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Mint a derived capability and link it under its source

steps.title: mint slot 4 → slot 5: asks for read + write, gets write
steps.narrative: Slot 4 carries write only; this asks for read and write. The kernel does not refuse: it masks the request with the source's rights, as seL4 does, so slot 5 receives write alone. A derived capability can never hold a right its source lacks, whatever it asks for. Slot 5 becomes a child of slot 4.

ipcBuffer.name: badge (message word 4; 0 keeps the source badge)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceMint invokes a CNode
Require the grant right
Decode the arm's 5 argument words
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Mint with the requested rights masked by the source's

steps.title: mint slot 1 → slot 5 (refused: slot occupied)
steps.narrative: Slot 5 already holds a capability. The destination is resolved before the source is even read, and a CNode operation never overwrites: the kernel refuses with targetSlotOccupied and every slot stays as it was.

ipcBuffer.name: badge (message word 4; 0 keeps the source badge)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceMint invokes a CNode
Require the grant right
Decode the arm's 5 argument words
Resolve the destination slot: it must be empty

steps.title: copy slot 4 → slot 6
steps.narrative: A copy keeps the source's badge and, with a mask of every right, its rights: a copy takes a rights mask too and can only narrow. Slot 6 becomes the first child of slot 4, in front of slot 5.

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceCopy invokes a CNode
Require the grant right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Copy the capability and link it under its source

steps.title: mint slot 1 → slot 8: read only, badge 9
steps.narrative: A second child of the master: read only, badge 9. A new child goes to the front of its parent's child list, so slot 1's children now read 8, then 4.

ipcBuffer.name: badge (message word 4; 0 keeps the source badge)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceMint invokes a CNode
Require the grant right
Decode the arm's 5 argument words
Source CNode → destination CNode flow check
Mint a derived capability and link it under its source

steps.title: delete slot 4
steps.narrative: Deleting a capability does not delete what was derived from it. Slot 4 is emptied and unlinked; its children, slots 6 and 5, take its place among the master's children, in their own order: 8, 6, 5. They keep their write right: revoking the master is still the way to take them back.

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceDelete invokes a CNode
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Delete the slot; its children take its place

steps.title: revoke slot 1
steps.narrative: Revoke deletes everything derived from slot 1 and keeps slot 1 itself. It repeatedly deletes the source's first child: slot 8, then slot 6, then slot 5. The master is left with no descendants.

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceRevoke invokes a CNode
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Delete the first child until none is left

scenarios.title: Carving and resetting untyped memory
scenarios.summary: All kernel memory starts as untyped regions. Retyping carves objects off a region at the free index of the untyped capability it is invoked through, each on its own alignment boundary; the index only rises until everything derived from that capability has been revoked, and only then can it be reset.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The memory manager holds a 16 KiB untyped region in slot 1 (with the retype right) and a capability to its own CNode in slot 0, where new capabilities land. Nothing has been carved yet: the capability's free index is 0.

steps.title: retype a 4 KiB frame into slot 2

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Check the capability's type: untypedRetype invokes an untyped
Require the retype right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words
Carve the object at the free index and install its capability

steps.narrative: x2 packs the object type (8, a frame) with its size bits (0: a frame is one page). The kernel carves 4 KiB at the free index, advances it to 4096, zeroes the page, and installs a frame capability in slot 2 as a child of the untyped capability, so revoking the untyped reaches it.

steps.title: retype an 8 KiB untyped into slot 3

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Check the capability's type: untypedRetype invokes an untyped
Require the retype right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words
Round the free index up, carve there and install the capability

steps.narrative: An untyped can be split into smaller untypeds: type 5 with 13 size bits is 8 KiB. A carve starts on a multiple of its own size, so the free index (4096) is rounded up to 8192: the 4 KiB between are skipped, the sub-untyped takes the upper half of the region, and the free index moves to 16384. The two children never overlap.

steps.title: retype another 8 KiB (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Check the capability's type: untypedRetype invokes an untyped
Require the retype right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words
Carve: 8192 bytes do not fit above the free index

steps.narrative: The free index is at the end of the region, so nothing fits above it: the 4 KiB skipped for alignment are not handed out either. The carve refuses with untypedRegionExhausted; the free index, the region's children and slot 4 are untouched.

steps.title: reset the untyped (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Check the capability's type: untypedReset invokes an untyped
Require the retype right
Reset: the capability still has derived children

steps.narrative: Resetting would hand the frame and the sub-untyped's memory out again while slots 2 and 3 still refer to them. The kernel refuses with revocationRequired while the untyped capability's slot has a derivation child: revoke first.

steps.title: revoke the untyped capability

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CNode)
Check the capability's type: cspaceRevoke invokes a CNode
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Delete the first child until none is left

steps.narrative: Every capability carved from the region is a child of the untyped capability, so revoking it deletes them: slot 3 first (the newest child is first), then slot 2. Each was the last capability to its object, so the objects themselves are retired and the region forgets them.

steps.title: reset the untyped

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the untyped)
Check the capability's type: untypedReset invokes an untyped
Require the retype right
Reset: write the capability's free index back to 0

steps.narrative: Nothing was derived from the capability any more and the region records no carved object, so the reset is one write: the capability's free index returns to 0. Nothing is scrubbed here; a frame is zeroed when it is next carved.

scenarios.title: Mapping pages under W^X
scenarios.summary: A thread maps code and data into its address space. A page may be writable or executable, never both: a request for both is refused while decoding the permission word. Unmapping a page also removes its cached translation.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The app's address space (ASID 1) already maps its stack, and the translation is cached. Slot 1 holds the address-space capability; slots 2–4 hold frame capabilities: code (read), data and scratch (read and write). Permission words are bits r=1, w=2, x=4, user=8, cacheable=16.

steps.title: map code read + execute

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Check the capability's type: vspaceMap invokes an address-space root
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words
Admit the frame, check the window and the walk, write the entry

steps.narrative: The permission word 0b11101 is read, execute, user and cacheable: W^X-compliant. The frame capability in slot 2 is looked up with read; a mapping that is not writable needs nothing more. The entry is written and the new translation is cached on the executing core.

steps.title: map data read + write

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Check the capability's type: vspaceMap invokes an address-space root
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words
Admit the frame, check the window and the walk, write the entry

steps.narrative: Read and write without execute: compliant. A writable mapping needs a frame capability carrying write, which slot 3 has.

steps.title: map scratch read + write + execute (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Check the capability's type: vspaceMap invokes an address-space root
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 4 argument words; the permissions are refused
Map the frame

steps.narrative: The address-space capability passes the gate: the arm then decodes its arguments, and 0b11111 is both writable and executable. PagePermissions.ofNat? has no value for such a word, so the decode refuses with invalidSyscallArgument and no entry is written.

steps.title: unmap the stack

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the address space)
Check the capability's type: vspaceUnmap invokes an address-space root
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 2 argument words
Clear the entry, shoot down the translation, invalidate the I-cache

steps.narrative: The entry is cleared and its cached translation is shot down on every core, so no core can still reach the frame through a stale TLB entry.

scenarios.title: Information flow and declassification
scenarios.summary: Security labels pair a confidentiality level with an integrity level. Information may flow to equal or higher confidentiality, and only to a destination at least as trusted as its source (the kernel's authority order, deliberately not Biba's). A secret thread is refused when it writes down; a public thread may write up; and a write down happens only through declassification, which a policy must authorize and the kernel records.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: sec (secret: high confidentiality, untrusted) runs; pub (public: low, untrusted) waits to run; rcv (secret) waits on the secret endpoint. The declassification policy authorizes secret → public and nothing else.

steps.title: sec: send to the public endpoint (refused)

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Check the capability's type: send invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send

steps.narrative: sec holds a perfectly good capability: the lookup and the rights check pass. But secret → public lowers confidentiality, so the flow gate refuses with flowDenied. Holding a capability is not enough; the labels must allow the flow as well.

steps.title: sec: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: sec yields and pub runs.

steps.title: pub: send to the secret endpoint

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1)
Check the capability's type: send invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send; a receiver waits, so deliver

steps.narrative: public → secret raises confidentiality and keeps integrity, so the flow is allowed. rcv is waiting on the endpoint and receives the word directly.

steps.title: pub: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: pub yields; sec is at the head of the bucket and runs.

steps.title: sec: declassify to the public endpoint

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the public endpoint)
Check the capability's type: declassify accepts any object capability
Require the write right
Authorize the downgrade and record it

steps.narrative: Declassification is for exactly the flows the lattice denies: secret → public is denied, and the policy authorizes it, so the kernel admits the downgrade. Its only effect is an entry in the audit log naming who downgraded what, from which label to which; it writes no object and edits no policy.

scenarios.title: Two cores and thread affinity
scenarios.summary: Each core has its own run queue and current thread. Rebinding a queued thread to another core moves its queue entry; rebinding a thread that is running on its old core takes it off that core and queues it on the new one, and the old core chooses again.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: w0 runs on core 0 and w1 on core 1, with 1 tick of its slice left. w2 and w3 wait in core 1's queue. w0 holds TCB capabilities to w3 (slot 2) and w1 (slot 3).

steps.title: w0: bind w3 to core 0

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, w3's TCB)
Check the capability's type: tcbSetAffinity invokes a thread
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Set the affinity and migrate the run-queue entry

steps.narrative: w3 is queued on core 1, not running, so its entry moves: out of core 1's queue and into core 0's. It does not preempt w0, whose priority is higher.

steps.title: w0: bind w1 to core 0 while it runs

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 3, w1's TCB)
Check the capability's type: tcbSetAffinity invokes a thread
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Set the affinity, vacate the old core and queue on the new one

steps.narrative: w1 is running on core 1. The change takes it off that core in the same transition: core 1's current thread is cleared and the core is flagged to choose again, and w1 joins core 0's run queue. It does not preempt w0, whose priority is equal. No other core resumes w1 until core 1 has saved its registers.

steps.title: core 1: chooses again
steps.narrative: Core 1 was left with no current thread and a pending reschedule. It picks from its own queue, where only w2 remains: w3 and w1 now belong to core 0.

scenarios.title: A device interrupt, from line to driver
scenarios.summary: A driver claims an interrupt line, binds a notification to it, and waits. The interrupt wakes the driver with the bound capability's badge and masks the line until the driver acknowledges it. A line nobody has claimed is masked and reaches no one.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The state the scenario starts from.

steps.title: line 33 fires with no handler
steps.narrative: No handler capability has been issued for line 33, so the line is not at IRQSignal and names no notification. The kernel does the one thing it can: it masks the line at the controller. Nothing is signalled and no thread is woken; an unclaimed device cannot interrupt the system twice.

steps.title: drv: claim line 33

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the interrupt-control capability)
Check the capability's type: irqControlGet invokes the interrupt-control capability
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 3 argument words
Check the line, then issue its handler capability

steps.narrative: The interrupt-control capability is the authority to hand out lines. The arm checks the line first (a device line of this board, with its node, held by no handler), then puts it at IRQSignal and installs a handler capability for line 33 in slot 3, as a derivation child of the control capability: revoking that capability reaches every handler it issued. The line stays masked; issuing a handler does not unmask it.

steps.title: drv: bind the notification to the line

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 3, the handler for line 33)
Check the capability's type: irqHandlerSetNotification invokes an interrupt-handler capability
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Copy the notification capability into the line's node

steps.narrative: x2 names the notification capability in the driver's own CSpace; it must be a notification capability with the send right. The kernel copies it, badge and all, into line 33's interrupt node: a one-slot CNode at a reserved id that no capability names. The copy is a derivation child of the driver's capability, so deleting or revoking that one unbinds the line. From now on the node slot is what an interrupt on line 33 reads.

steps.title: drv: acknowledge, unmasking the line

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 3, the handler for line 33)
Check the capability's type: irqHandlerAck invokes an interrupt-handler capability
Require the write right
Unmask the line at the controller

steps.narrative: The line has been masked since it fired with no handler. An acknowledge writes exactly one thing: the line's mask, cleared. The device can interrupt again.

steps.title: drv: wait for the device

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, the notification)
Check the capability's type: notificationWait invokes a notification
Require the read right
Notification → waiter flow gate
Wait; the word is clear, so block

steps.narrative: Nothing is pending on the notification, so the driver joins its wait queue and leaves the core.

steps.title: core 0: the application runs
steps.narrative: The driver left the core, so the scheduler picks again. The application is the only runnable thread.

steps.title: line 33 fires: the driver is woken
steps.narrative: The controller raises line 33 on core 0 while the application runs. The kernel acknowledges and ends the interrupt at the controller, then reads the line's node slot: a notification capability with the send right, badge 4. That notification is signalled with that badge. The driver is the head of its wait queue, so it is taken off, made ready with the badge in its message, and queued on its home core. The line is then masked: it will not fire again until the driver acknowledges it.

steps.title: core 0: the driver preempts
steps.narrative: The wake flagged core 0 to choose again. The best candidate is the driver at priority 120; the application runs at 50, so the candidate outranks it. The application goes to the tail of the run queue and the driver runs.

steps.title: drv: service the device and acknowledge

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 3, the handler for line 33)
Check the capability's type: irqHandlerAck invokes an interrupt-handler capability
Require the write right
Unmask the line at the controller

steps.narrative: The driver has handled the device. Its acknowledge unmasks line 33, and the next interrupt can be delivered.

steps.title: drv: claim line 33 a second time

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the interrupt-control capability)
Check the capability's type: irqControlGet invokes the interrupt-control capability
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 3 argument words
Check the line: a handler already holds it

steps.narrative: Every gate passes: the capability is the interrupt-control capability and carries the write right, and the message is long enough. The arm's own first check refuses: line 33 is already at IRQSignal, so a handler holds it, and a second handler for one line would be a second owner. The refusal comes before any slot is resolved and nothing is written.

steps.title: drv: acknowledge through the wrong capability

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, the notification)
Check the capability's type: irqHandlerAck invokes an interrupt-handler capability
Require the write right
Unmask the line at the controller

steps.narrative: Slot 2 holds a capability, and it even carries the write right an acknowledge asks for. But it is a notification capability, and an acknowledge invokes an interrupt handler. The type gate runs after the lookup and before any right, so a capability of the wrong type is refused as invalid whatever rights it carries.

scenarios.title: Passing a capability through IPC
scenarios.summary: A client sends a frame capability to a server along with a message. The endpoint capability it sends through decides whether the capability travels: without the grant right the message arrives alone. A transferred capability is a copy, recorded under the slot it came from, so revoking the original takes the copy back.

steps.title: Initial state
steps.narrative: The state the scenario starts from.

steps.title: client: send a capability without the grant right

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 2, the endpoint without grant)
Check the capability's type: send invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send; a receiver waits, so deliver

steps.narrative: x1 says the message carries one extra capability, and the client's IPC buffer names it: address 3, the frame. The send itself is allowed: slot 2 is an endpoint capability with the write right. But transferring a capability needs the grant right on the endpoint capability, and slot 2 does not carry it. A sender without grant transfers nothing, and its addresses are not even looked up. The server receives the message word and no capability; its receive slot stays empty.

steps.title: client: yield

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Charge the rest of the slice, requeue at the tail, pick again

steps.narrative: The client gives up the core so the server can run. Yield names no capability, so the path goes straight from decode to the scheduler.

steps.title: server: receive again

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the endpoint)
Check the capability's type: receive invokes an endpoint
Require the read right
Endpoint → receiver flow gate
Receive; nothing is queued, so block

steps.narrative: The server has handled the first message and waits for the next. No sender is queued, so it joins the endpoint's receive queue and leaves the core. Its IPC buffer still names slot 4 of its CSpace as the place a transferred capability should land.

steps.title: core 0: the client resumes
steps.narrative: The server left the core, so the scheduler picks again: the client.

steps.title: client: send the capability with grant

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 1, the endpoint with grant)
Check the capability's type: send invokes an endpoint
Require the write right
Sender → endpoint flow gate
Send; a receiver waits, so deliver

steps.narrative: The same message through slot 1, which carries grant. Now the kernel resolves address 3 in the client's CSpace and finds the frame capability. It is not a capability to the endpoint itself (that would be unwrapped to its badge), so it is installed in the server's receive slot, slot 4 of the server's CSpace. The server gets the same capability with the same rights; the client keeps its own. The derivation tree records the server's slot as a child of the client's slot 3.

steps.title: client: revoke what it handed out

path.label: Checked syscall entry
Decode x0, x1 and x7 from the register file
Resolve x0 in the caller's CSpace (slot 0, the CSpace root)
Check the capability's type: cspaceRevoke invokes a CNode
Require the write right
Decode the arm's 1 argument word
Delete every capability derived from the slot

steps.narrative: The client revokes slot 3. Revocation deletes every capability derived from the slot and keeps the slot's own. The only derivation is the copy in the server's CSpace, in another thread's CNode, and it is deleted: the server can no longer reach the frame. This is why the transfer recorded a derivation edge instead of handing over an unrelated copy.
